archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A Boston team whose point margin and efficiency profile belong among the league's top three or four, but whose 11-6 record trails what that margin implies, and which now wins with defense rather than the shot-making that defined its recent seasons.

report.headline: An elite defense with a misleading record, now testing life without Paul George.
report.take:
These are not the Celtics of the last few years. From 2022-23 through 2025-26 Boston ran a top-two offense every season and a defense that hovered between third and fifth. This year the order has flipped. The defense ranks 3rd with a 107.2 defensive rating against a league average of 114.4, close to the 106.9 the 2021-22 team posted. The offense has slid to 9th at 116.7, down from 120.8 last season. Boston allows 102.12 points a game, the fewest in the league. Some of that comes from the league's crawl of a pace, 94.7, but the per-possession numbers say the defense is genuinely elite.

The defense is built on keeping opponents out of the paint. Only 23.9% of opponent shots come at the rim (3rd), and those that do go in at 61% (4th). Opponents post a 50.2 eFG % (2nd) and turn it over 15.3 times per 100 plays (4th). By position, opposing centers have been held to their lowest production relative to their own averages anywhere in the league. The offense is more ordinary than its reputation. Boston still lives behind the arc, with a 50.5 3PA Rate (2nd), and it pounds the offensive glass (31 ORB %, 3rd). But its TS % ranks 22nd and its FT Rate 25th, so it rarely gets cheap points. Jayson Tatum carries a 32.9 USG % and is the No. 2 small forward on the site. The guards around him are less efficient: Derrick White sits at a 51.5 TS %, Payton Pritchard at 53.4.

The record understates the team. The point differential implies 13 wins, not 11, and the W vs Pt Diff of -2 ranks 26th. The current skid shows this plainly. Boston went 1-4 over the last five games yet outscored opponents by 21 in that stretch. The four losses came by small margins, including 96-97 at Sacramento and 87-88 at Golden State. Close-game misfortune has been a Boston habit: W vs Pt Diff was negative in four of the last five seasons. That suggests it is partly a pattern, but it is still mostly noise. The bigger worry is that scoring has dried up. Boston scored 120.8 a game in October, 107.25 in November and 104 over the last five games. Paul George is now listed out, and he carries a +14.7 On-Off and ranks No. 2 among power forwards. Mitchell Robinson is also out, though his -23.8 On-Off says that one costs little.

The floor is high because the defense travels and the margin is real. The ceiling depends on whether the half-court offense can function with Tatum doing even more. The best lineup signal is the frontcourt pairing of Neemias Queta (+22.4 On-Off, 61.8 TS %) and Sam Hauser (+14.2, 64.5 TS %). Minutes that drift to Jordan Walsh (-15.8) are the soft spot without George. The site has Boston 6th, which looks about right: a clear playoff team on a 53-win pace whose results should catch up to its margin.

strengths.title: Paint-denial defense, league-best scoring defense
strengths.body: Boston allows the fewest points a game in the league and owns the 3rd-best defensive rating. It gets there by keeping teams away from the rim and contesting everything else. The opponent rim rate and eFG % both sit near the top of the league, and centers are the position Boston suppresses most relative to their own averages. The defensive rating is better than any of the last four seasons, so some drift upward is likely. Still, the paint-denial pattern held in 2025-26 too, which says it is structural.

strengths.title: Margin of a top-three team
strengths.body: Boston's Net Rtg ranks 3rd, and the differential implies 13 wins against the actual 11. Even during a 1-4 stretch, it outscored opponents by 21. Records tend to follow margins over a long season, so the wins should come.

strengths.title: Tatum plus an efficient Queta-Hauser core
strengths.body: Tatum is the No. 2 small forward on the site, with a 6.3 BPM on heavy usage. Queta and Hauser are the most efficient regulars and post the best On-Off numbers on the roster. With George out, those three are the reliable part of the rotation.

concerns.title: Offense shrinking with George out
concerns.body: Scoring fell from 120.8 a game in October to 107.25 in November, and to 104 over the last five games. George, the club's No. 2 option and a +14.7 On-Off player, is listed out. Boston takes threes at an extreme rate but ranks low in TS % and FT Rate, so cold shooting nights leave nothing to fall back on.

concerns.title: Leaky defensive rebounding
concerns.body: For a defense this good, Boston finishes possessions poorly. Its DRB % ranks 21st, well below the 75-78 range of recent seasons. Opposing power forwards collect more rebounds than they average elsewhere, one of the worst marks in the league on that measure. Crashing the offensive glass may be part of the trade-off. Against big rebounding teams, it is the crack in the defense.

concerns.title: Inefficient guard play
concerns.body: The backcourt grades C+. White and Pritchard split the guard minutes almost evenly, and both shoot below league-average efficiency. Pritchard's -10.6 On-Off is a red flag on a team this good. Mike Conley's hot six-game start is far too small a sample to count on.

trend.note: A 4-1 October gave way to a six-game winning streak in early November, then four straight narrow losses on the road. The margin stayed strong throughout, while the scoring steadily dipped.

weekAhead.headline: Two soft interiors, then San Antonio and Dallas back-to-back on the road.
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with games Boston should win. Washington ranks 21st on the site with the 21st-ranked defense. Atlanta matches Boston at 11-6, but its interior is the weakest part of a good defense. Both teams give up plenty of rim attempts. That gives a Boston offense starved for easy points a chance to get Queta going and reach the line.

Then it turns hard. The trip ends at San Antonio, 14-3 with the league's best Net Rtg, and at Dallas the next night. Dallas is 10-7 on a roughly even margin and a W vs Pt Diff of +2, and Boston beat it 131-94 two weeks ago. Two wins out of four is the floor and three is the realistic goal. Note that three of the four games are on the road and the last two are a back-to-back.

keyMatchups.title: Attacking the rim early in the week
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows the 3rd-highest share of shots at the rim and ranks 26th in rim defense, and centers feast against it. Washington also ranks 25th in opponent rim rate. This is the best chance all month for Queta and for a team that rarely gets to the line.

keyMatchups.title: San Antonio's defense versus Boston's bigs
keyMatchups.body: The Spurs have the 2nd-best defensive rating and allow the fewest points to power forwards, so Hauser's spot-up looks may be scarce. Centers, though, score well above their averages against San Antonio, which points the offense toward Queta. The Spurs also lead the league in rebounds per game, a direct test of Boston's weak defensive glass.

keyMatchups.title: Dallas on the second night
keyMatchups.body: Dallas's record runs ahead of its margin, and its 24th-ranked DRB % suits Boston's offensive rebounding. Fatigue on the second night of a back-to-back is the main threat.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Boston's scoring climbs back from the 104 a game of its last five against the soft interiors of Washington and Atlanta.

restOfSeason.body:
The margin is the best guide here, and it points to a team that wins more than its record suggests. Close-game losses tend to even out, though Boston's history of negative W vs Pt Diff suggests it may not fully reverse. The defense is the sustainable part: the paint-denial profile carried over from last season. The defensive rating will probably drift toward the 108-110.5 range rather than stay at 107.2. The offense should recover somewhat toward 116-119 once George returns, because a team this reliant on threes will see its shooting swing back.

The overall range is 50 to 56 wins. That puts Boston in the top tier of the East behind or alongside Philadelphia, without the elite offense that made earlier Boston teams favorites.
swingFactors: How long Paul George is out and how he looks on return

confidence.note: Only 17 games played, and two rotation players are now out, but the margin and defensive profile are strong signals.
